title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 226 (Voluntary winding up of company, etc., not to stop investigation proceedings)

content.overview: Section 226 provides that an investigation under this Chapter may be initiated or continued notwithstanding that an application has been made under section 241, or a special resolution has been passed for voluntary winding up, or any other proceeding for the winding up of the company is pending before the Tribunal. Where a winding-up order is made, the inspector must inform the liquidator of any pending investigation, and the liquidator must give the inspector all assistance. The section prevents a company from ending an inquiry by resolving to wind up.
content.glance: Investigation may be initiated or continued despite pending s. 241 application, voluntary winding-up resolution, or other winding-up proceedings; liquidator must assist the inspector.
content.study: An investigation under this Chapter may be initiated notwithstanding that an application has been made under section 241 or that a special resolution has been passed for the voluntary winding up of the company or that any other proceeding for the winding up of the company is pending before the Tribunal. Where a winding-up order has been made or a provisional liquidator has been appointed, the inspector shall inform the liquidator of any investigation pending, and the liquidator shall give the inspector all assistance. Current-law framing: confirm that winding-up steps do not bar initiation or continuation of Chapter XIV investigation; require liquidator assistance where a winding-up order or provisional liquidator is in place. Note: voluntary winding up under the Companies Act has largely given way to IBC processes; the section still states that investigation is not stopped by winding-up proceedings.

sections.heading: Non-Stop Rule
sections.body: Investigation may be initiated or continued despite: application under s. 241; special resolution for voluntary winding up; or other winding-up proceedings pending before the Tribunal.

sections.heading: Liquidator Duty
sections.body: Where a winding-up order is made or a provisional liquidator appointed, the inspector informs the liquidator; the liquidator must give all assistance to the investigation.

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.body: Prevents a company from ending an inquiry by resolving to wind up or by pending winding-up process.

provisions.title: Voluntary winding up of company, etc., not to stop investigation proceedings

examples.title: Investigation after voluntary resolution
examples.body: Members pass a special resolution for voluntary winding up while a s. 210 investigation is ongoing. Under s. 226 the investigation may continue.

examples.title: Liquidator assistance
examples.body: A winding-up order is made during a pending investigation. The inspector informs the liquidator under s. 226; the liquidator must assist the inspector.

hypotheticals.question: Does a winding-up petition automatically terminate a Chapter XIV investigation?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 226 expressly provides that investigation may be initiated or continued notwithstanding pending winding-up proceedings. The liquidator must assist.

distinctions.title: Investigation not stopped by winding up (s. 226) vs CG petition for winding up on report (s. 224)
distinctions.right: CG may present a winding-up petition based on inspector’s report

misconceptions.trap: Once a company resolves to wind up, all statutory investigations must stop.
misconceptions.correction: Section 226 provides that investigation under Chapter XIV may be initiated or continued notwithstanding a voluntary winding-up resolution or pending winding-up proceedings.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 226 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify investigation status. II. Note winding-up step does not stop it. III. Apply liquidator assistance if ordered. IV. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Investigation facts; winding-up status; non-stop rule; assistance duty; precise relief.
